hooks.command:
jq -r '.tool_input.command' | { read -r cmd; if echo "$cmd" | grep -qE 'expense_tracker\.db' && echo "$cmd" | grep -qE '(^|[^a-zA-Z])(rm|mv|truncate|unlink|dd|shred)([^a-zA-Z]|$)|>[[:space:]]*expense_tracker\.db'; then jq -cn '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:"🚫  Action blocked — database is protected

This command would delete or overwrite expense_tracker.db, the Spendly app database that holds real user data.

A project safety hook stops destructive commands (rm, mv, truncate, dd, shred, redirect >) from touching this file.

If you genuinely need a clean database, delete it yourself outside Claude Code, then ask Claude to reinitialize it with init_db()."}}'; else echo '{}'; fi; }
